verdict.rationale: Rootly documents the incident timeline as an authoritative chronological record that brings together updates from people, systems, automations, and communication channels. That covers automatic capture of alerts, actions, and chat. Post-incident editing is evidenced only indirectly: a Curated Timeline section is auto-drafted in retrospectives from incident data and Slack, and that section can be edited in the collaborative editor. Missing for 10: documented direct editing or annotation of the incident timeline itself, explicit confirmation that alerts and chat decisions land as timeline entries, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, the incident timeline is captured automatically — alerts, actions, and chat decisions — and I can edit or annotate it afterwards

citations.quote: It brings together updates from people, systems, automations, and communication channels into one clear, chronological narrative.
sections like Summary, Impact, Root Cause, Mitigation, Resolution, and Curated Timeline get drafted automatically from the incident's data, Slack channel, and bridge-call transcripts
Insert Rootly AI blocks in a retrospective, watch them generate, inspect their sources, and edit, regenerate, convert, or rate the output.
